identification: Long live-edge slab of Tasmanian myrtle (Nothofagus cunninghamii), about 2.2 to 2.4 m, narrow (roughly 25 to 35 cm) with a flared, knotty lower end; chalk 1108 and dated 30/10/26; second from left in a row of near identical slabs (1107, 1109 alongside). Rough sawn, some sapwood and end checking at top. Not a wide figured showpiece; looks like the ordinary run of Gowans myrtle slabs. Photo count 1, no dimensions or thickness stated.

searches_tried: comps.py (pipeline and work) with myrtle slab, myrtle live edge, tasmanian myrtle; Gowans API search 'myrtle slab' (past results, 40 lots, hammer prices in cents converted; the 6 lots 447515-447520 and 447844/447859 are this sale, skipped); WebSearch 'Tasmanian myrtle live edge slab for sale price'. Armitage site search not run (rule: no Armitage lot pages). eBay sold prices not reachable; would help only marginally. Gowans history is the best evidence: about 40 comparable lots, median about $45, middle half roughly $20 to $85 hammer, top $125 for a single slab.
viewing_check: Check thickness (40 mm+ is worth more), width at the narrowest point, length, depth and extent of end checks and splits, whether the figure/burl is real or surface staining, sapwood and bark pockets, borer holes, and how dry it is. Compare against 1107 and 1109 which look very similar. Oct 25 sale showed single slabs reaching $95 to $125 hammer, so the best slabs are the thick, wide, clean ones.
